{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "Willingness to pay is better evidenced. B's competitors publish paid tiers at every level: NeverFined at $29–99/mo, ExpirationOps at $49/mo, and ClearBot at $500–800/location/yr. Harbor Compliance has 212 Google reviews, which suggests real paying users. In A, two of five competitors are fully free or have pricing marked NOT FOUND, and WeGoUp is pre-alpha.",
    "B's need recurs and A's does not. Renewal cycles, audit dates and rule changes come back every year, which supports retention. A's brief admits the need 'ends at re-employment,' which caps lifetime value.",
    "B's unit economics look more workable. Its buyer is a business paying from an ops or compliance budget at $29–99/mo or more, against $10–14.50 CPC plus SEO content. A sells at $8–24/mo to a segment its own brief calls financially strained and price-sensitive, while Google cost per lead in the category is $117.92 (2024).",
    "B carries lower harm and liability risk for a lightly supervised AI operation. Competitors have already proven a 'tracking only, not advice' posture. A handles sensitive health, caregiving and disability context and gives 'trajectory' advice, so poor output has real reputational and harm risk.",
    "Both markets are crowded, so neither idea wins on greenfield. B at least shows a reachable SMB tier where small SEO-driven operators appear to sell. A faces free alternatives such as GapZero and general-purpose ChatGPT."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's demand evidence shows anxiety, not purchase intent. None of the forum quotes shows anyone paying for gap reframing. The strongest quote (every.to) cuts against the idea: the person explicitly substitutes an existing ChatGPT subscription for paid help, implying a general LLM already meets the need for free. Separately, the stated '$62–$118 CPL' range is derived from a percentage decline rather than directly sourced, and free-to-paid conversion is admitted to be unverified.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. B wins mainly on payer quality, recurring need and lower risk, but its own case against is serious. Seven-plus competitors run the same SEO playbook, and nothing in the brief identifies a wedge. A six-week build likely yields a static tracker that is a subset of $29–49/mo incumbents. The RegTech $14.50 CPC figure has no link and is treated as missing. Neither brief offers conversion or retention data, so B's edge rests on structural factors rather than proven traction."
}
